MIND. [1] [Bar. m.]
Idiocy.
In every form of mania, as soon as the sexual desire is increased.
Great anxiety, with pressure in stomach, nausea and retching ; has to bend double.
Appears like an epileptic, with full consciousness. θ Induration of pancreas.
   

SENSORIUM. [2] [Bar. m.]
Vertigo ; things turn around.
   

OUTER HEAD. [4] [Bar. m.]
Tinea capitis extending to sides and posterior portion of neck.
Tinea, with abundant discharge of pus.
The whole scalp covered by a thick, offensive crust. θ Scrofulous ulcers.
   

SIGHT AND EYES. [5] [Bar. m.]
Shuns light, child lies all the time on its face. θ Scrofulous ulcers.
Eyeballs much inflamed. θ Scrofulous ulcers.
Lids on both eyes swollen and inflamed. θ Scrofulous ulcers.
Ophthalmia scrofulosis.
Staphyloma spurium with a boy, æt. 9, on inner edge of l. cornea.
Hernia tunicæ humoris aquei.
   

HEARING AND EARS. [6] [Bar. m.]
Ears pain. θ Angina.
Catarrh of ears.
Discharge from both ears of an odor like rotten cheese.
Otorrhœa after frequent otitis.
Post-scarlatinal otorrhœa.
Profuse purulent otorrhœa of five years' standing.
Otorrhœa on both sides, offensive discharge. θ Glandular swelling.
Abscess behind both ears, discharging offensive pus. θ Scrofulous ulcers.
Parotis on right side swollen, with a swelling of submaxillary and cervical glands.
Both parotids, most right side, swell after scarlatina.
Parotis swollen hard, not very painful, but extending to edge of lower maxilla.
   

SMELL AND NOSE. [7] [Bar. m.]
Catarrh of nose.
   

LOWER FACE. [9] [Bar. m.]
Enlarged, indurated and painful submaxillary glands. θ Otorrhœa.
   

TASTE, SPEECH, TONGUE. [11] [Bar. m.]
Tongue furred. θ Glandular swelling.
Tongue covered with mucus.
   

INNER MOUTH. [12] [Bar. m.]
Great salivation. θ Angina.
   

PALATE AND THROAT. [13] [Bar. m.]
Elongation of uvula, with hyperemia and blennorrhœa. θ Angina tonsillaris.
Inner throat hyperemic and blennorrheic.
Varicose veins in throat.
Catarrh extends over tonsils, epiglottis, glottis, into tubes. θ Angina tonsillaris.
Angina tonsillaris, with suppuration, after every cold, with variola or varioloid.
Severe pain in right side of throat and ear ; saliva ran from mouth in large quantities ; fauces, especially on right side, of a deep red color ; tonsils but little swollen. θ Angina.
In a girl, both tonsils enlarged ; chills and heat alternately with general malaise, headache, thirst, etc. ; pulse 120 ; deglutition painful on right side, extending to ear ; tonsil red. θ Chronic hypertrophy of tonsils.
Disposition to tonsillitis, with suppuration each time after taking cold.
Chronic scrofulous enlargement and induration of tonsils.
   

APPETITE, THIRST. DESIRES, AVERSIONS. [14] [Bar. m.]
Increased appetite.
Appetite diminished. θ Glandular swelling.
Desire for dry wheat bread.
Glandular swelling.
Thirst ; chill and fever alternately. θ Angina.
   

HICCOUGH, BELCHING, NAUSEA AND VOMITING. [16] [Bar. m.]
Nausea, with vomiting and violent colic. θ Hydrops.
Nausea, vomiting, with worms and colic. θ After scarlatina.
   

SCROBICULUM AND STOMACH. [17] [Bar. m.]
Great indigestion.
Inflammation of stomach.
Below stomach to left side a hardness, from which paroxysms of want of breath originate. θ Induration of pancreas.
Considerable hardness in region of stomach.
   

HYPOCHONDRIA. [18] [Bar. m.]
Tumefaction of liver.
   

ABDOMEN AND LOINS. [19] [Bar. m.]
Pain in region of navel ; < in morning ; dry cough ; great appetite ; slime-covered tongue. θ Ascarides.
Distressing throbbing in a tumor inside of abdomen. θ Abdominal aneurism.
Abdomen much swollen. θ Scrofulous ulcers.
Abdomen distended. θ Glandular swelling.
Swelling of abdomen and lower limbs. θ After scarlatina.
Abdomen distended and hard. θ Scrofulosis glandulosa.
   

STOOLS AND RECTUM. [20] [Bar. m.]
Obstinate constipation.
Stools of a jelly-like appearance, with blood, no pain at all, discharges every 15 or 20 minutes. θ Dysentery.
Bloody, mucous stools, without much pain, several times a day ; child. θ Dysentery.
Colic and several stools ; boy, æt. 9.
Thin, watery, very fetid stools. θ Scrofulous ulcers.
Stool only after injections, excrement white and hard as stones. θ Scrofulous glands.
   

URINARY ORGANS. [21] [Bar. m.]
Cystitis.
Urine yellowish, of a very offensive odor. θ Glandular swelling.
Urine yellowish, of great stench. θ Scrofulous glands.
   

MALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [22] [Bar. m.]
Sexual desire. See 1.
Gonorrhœa and gleet.
Hypertrophied testicle after suppressed gonorrhœa.
Testicles increased in size, hard and painful stitches ; for nine years.
Swelling of testicles and scrotum, painless. θ After a contusion while riding on horseback.
Buboes after suppressed gonorrhœa.
   

FEMALE SEXUAL ORGANS. [23] [Bar. m.]
Sterility.
Leucorrhœa.
Induration, tumor, or atrophy of ovaries.
Nymphomania.
   

RESPIRATION. [26] [Bar. m.]
Attacks of anxious dyspnœa ; rolls on floor, several attacks a day, also in night. θ Epilepsy, with full consciousness.
Has to sit up, head bent forward ; slime and saliva runs from mouth, without cough. θ Induration of pancreas.
   

COUGH. [27] [Bar. m.]
Dry cough.
Chronic cough of scrofulous children.
   

INNER CHEST AND LUNGS. [28] [Bar. m.]
Blennorrhœa of lungs with scrofula.
Phthisis scrofulosa, with herpetic eruption and indurated testicle.
   

HEART, PULSE AND CIRCULATION. [29] [Bar. m.]
Pulse 120. θ Angina.
Abdominal aneurism.
   

NECK AND BACK. [31] [Bar. m.]
Beginning struma ; child, æt. 6 months, breathing with a rattle.
The whole neck and throat full of hard glandular swellings, size of eggs.
Enlargement and induration of cervical glands. θ Otorrhœa.
Submaxillary and cervical glands swollen to size of pigeon eggs, two like hen's eggs, very hard, and painful on slight pressure. θ Swelling of parotis.
Two cervical glands swollen and fluctuating. θ Swelling of parotids.
Vertebræ 7 and 8 are protruding, forming a hump. θ Glandular swelling, scrofula.
Tinea from scalp to neck.
   

LOWER LIMBS. [33] [Bar. m.]
When kneeling, a violent stitch, followed by a peculiar tension in right patella, making it difficult to walk. θ Hemorrhagic extravasation of knee.
Tension and increased warmth in knee. θ Swelling of knee.
A globular swelling on tip of right knee, increasing quickly but without much pain. θ Hemorrhagic swelling of knee.
A round, sharply defined swelling, size of a goose egg, of a dark color and clearly fluctuating, surrounded by bluish-red spots, not disappearing on pressure, with a greenish-yellow halo. θ Hemorrhagic extravasation.
Hemorrhagic extravasation in bursa patellæ.
After checking foot sweat. θ Tonsillitis.
Feet swollen. θ Glandular swelling.
   

LIMBS IN GENERAL. [34] [Bar. m.]
Paralysis of upper and lower limbs.
   

REST. POSITION. MOTION. [35] [Bar. m.]
Neither motion nor pressure is painful. θ Gonitis.
   

NERVES. [36] [Bar. m.]
Paralysis of left side, with aphasia.
General malaise. θ Angina.
   

TEMPERATURE AND WEATHER. [39] [Bar. m.]
Spring and Fall attacks of angina tonsillaris.
   

FEVER. [40] [Bar. m.]
Tertian intermittent.
Chills with heat, alternately with angina tonsillaris.
   

TISSUES. [44] [Bar. m.]
Varicose veins. θ Angina tonsillaris.
Affection of lymphatic vessels and glands in scrofula.
Hydrops after scarlatina.
Painful glandular swellings and indurations of scrofulous people.
Adenitis.
Catarrhal affections.
Pale and emaciated. θ Dysentery.
Emaciation. θ Swelling of cervical glands.
   

TOUCH. PASSIVE MOTION. INJURIES. [45] [Bar. m.]
Swelling of testicle and scrotum from bruising, caused by riding horseback.
   

SKIN. [46] [Bar. m.]
Skin not reddened, not warmer than usual. θ Swelling of parotis.
Itch-like pimples on head, nape of neck, abdomen and thighs.
Yellowish, scaly eruptions.
Herpes on various parts. θ Hypertrophy of testicle.
Herpes favinosus all over body, face excepted.
Tetters.
Scrofulous eruptions.
Whole body covered with ulcers. θ Scrofula.
Complaints after scarlet fever.
   

STAGE OF LIFE, CONSTITUTION. [47] [Bar. m.]
Scrofulous children. See 13, 27, 31.
Child, æt. 18 months. θ Dysentery after humid tetter.
Girl, æt. 18 months. θ Scrofulous ulcers.
Boy, æt. 2, scrofulous, emaciated. θ Indurated cervical glands.
Boy, æt. 4, three weeks after scarlatina. θ Swelling of parotis.
Blonde, blue-eyed girl. θ Earache.
Scrofulous child, æt. 10, since five years otorrhœa and glandular swellings, cured by one dose daily for two weeks.
Girls, æt. 39. θ Hemorrhagic extravasation of knee.
Man, æt. 50, strong constitution, inclined to catarrhal affections, and great disposition to angina tonsillaris.
Woman, æt. 53, small, weakly, poorly fed. θ Parotid swelling.
Woman, æt. 65, after five months absolute rest and strict diet having been useless, 1/5 grain in distilled water, three times daily, for several weeks. θ Abdominal aneurism.
